draft_context.source_title: iOS 27: Release date, Beta, compatible iPhones and all new features
draft_context.description: Macworld Apple has officially unveiled the new features coming to compatible iPhones running iOS 27 later this year, introducing major Apple Intelligence upgrades, changes to Siri, parental controls enhancements and improvements across core iPhone apps. iOS 27 is currently available as a beta test version for developers and public testers. The software has been going through several months of testing before its full public release – which is likely to happen in the next few weeks. Apple typically launches new versions of iOS in September, often around the second week – making Monday, September 14 a likely release date based on past patterns. iOS 27 will be supported on every iPhone all the way back to iPhone 11 and iPhone SE 2, though some Apple Intelligence and Siri related features will only be available on newer iPhones. This hub contains everything Apple has confirmed will be coming in iOS 27 when it launches, including new features, compatible iPhones, beta release information, Apple Intelligence updates and what’s new for Siri. What’s New in iOS 27 at a Glance Siri AI : Apple’s new Siri AI combines personal context, onscreen awareness and web knowledge to deliver more natural conversations, richer answers, app actions and cross-device chat history. Apple Intelligence across apps : Apple Intelligence expands across Safari, Photos, Messages, Mail, Calendar, Home and Shortcuts, adding smarter suggestions, automation, image generation and context-aware assistance. Smarter Photos editing : Photos gains Spatial Reframing, Extend and an upgraded Clean Up tool, allowing users to improve composition, expand images and remove distractions more naturally. Child safety and parental controls : New parental controls include Ask to Browse, Time Allowances, app schedules and enhanced Communication Safety tools designed to give parents more control. Safari and productivity upgrades : Safari can organise tabs, monitor webpages and build extensions from descriptions, while Passwords, Calendar and Shortcuts gain powerful new AI-powered capabilities. iOS 27 release date: When will Apple release iOS 27? September 2026 iOS 27 has been in beta since it was unveiled at WWDC in June, but the official version of iOS 27 will not be available to install on compatible iPhones until later in 2026. Apple has confirmed that the iPhone launch event will take place on September 9, so we anticipate that iOS 27 will be available to download on Monday, September 14, as the iOS download usually closely follows Apple’s September event. What is the latest iOS 27 beta? As of September 1, iOS 27 beta 8 is now available to developers, with the public beta expected shortly. At this late stage in the development cycle, Apple is focusing on stability rather than adding new features, with recent betas mainly delivering bug fixes, security updates, performance improvements and final polish ahead of launch. Siri AI in iOS 27 Apple By far the biggest upgrade coming in iOS 27 is Siri AI – Apple’s new Apple Intelligence-powered version of Siri. Apple says it is more personal, conversational and capable than the current assistant, with support for natural follow-up questions, personal context, onscreen awareness and up-to-date information from the web. Siri AI features More natural conversations : Siri AI can understand open-ended questions, follow-up requests and more complex natural language, making interactions feel less like issuing simple voice commands. Personal context : Siri can draw on information stored in Messages, Mail, Photos and Notes to find details and answer questions. For example, you could ask it to find information buried in an old email or message. Onscreen awareness : Siri can understand what you’re viewing and act on it, such as saving an address from a message, adding an event to Calendar or answering questions about an article. Camera intelligence : A new Siri Camera mode lets you show Siri something through the iPhone’s camera, then ask questions or perform actions based on what it sees. More capable app actions : Siri can perform tasks within apps such as Messages, Music and Reminders. It can, for example, edit a recently sent message, add a song to a playlist or handle more complex Apple Music requests. Better general knowledge and web answers : Siri can use information from the web to answer questions about recent events and tackle more specific or complicated queries than before. Conversation history across devices : A dedicated Siri app lets users revisit previous conversations, pin important chats and continue conversations across Apple devices using iCloud syncing. More natural Siri voices : Siri gains more expressive voices, with controls on compatible devices for adjusting speaking pace and expressiveness. Voice customisation requires an iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone Air or newer. Improved dictation : Better speech recognition, automatic punctuation, capitalisation and formatting allow users to dictate more naturally when converting speech into text. AI-assisted message replies : Siri can compose contextual replies in Messages using the conversation, personal information and web searches. Shortcuts can also automate replies to selected contacts, although manual Siri-assisted replies allow users to check and edit the response before it is sent. For more Siri AI message replies read about what happened when we made Siri AI Answer all our Messages . How good is Siri AI? Siri AI represents a significant improvement over the old Siri, particularly when handling conversational questions, current information and personal context. Early testing suggests it can deal with far more complicated requests than Siri previously could. Apple Music is a good example: Siri can identify very specific groups of songs, create playlists and combine music knowledge with reasoning. It could therefore become one of the biggest reasons to upgrade to iOS 27, potentially changing Siri from a basic voice-command system into a more general way of interacting with the iPhone. However, Siri AI is still in beta. Testing has revealed server failures, incorrect answers, weak reasoning and unexplained limitations, so its usefulness will depend heavily on how much Apple improves reliability before release. Apple’s approach to AI safety also appears more restrained than some rival chatbots, with Siri designed to avoid excessive flattery, pretending to be human or responding inappropriately to potentially harmful requests. When will Siri AI launch? Apple says iOS 27 arrives in autumn 2026, but Siri AI does not yet have a specific public release date. Apple currently says the new Siri will launch in English later in 2026. Regional Siri AI availability Siri AI will not initially be available on iPhone or iPad in the EU. It will also remain unavailable in China while Apple works through regulatory issues. Siri AI compatibility Some Siri AI features have more demanding hardware requirements than others. In particular, Apple’s new Siri voice customisation controls require an iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone Air or newer. Apple Intelligence across apps As well as Siri AI, the enhanced Apple Intelligence will also power new AI-powered features in Apple’s core apps throughout iOS 27. Safari will organise tabs into topics, monitor webpages for changes and even build extensions from natural-language descriptions. Photos is set to gain a new Spatial Reframing edit tools including and an upgraded Clean Up feature. Messages, Mail and Calendar will be able to understand context, suggest actions and create events from simple descriptions. New features coming to apps in iOS 27 iOS 27 brings a mix of major Apple Intelligence upgrades and smaller quality-of-life improvements across Safari, Photos, Messages, AirPods, Passwords, Wallet and other core iPhone apps. Apple is also making iOS more adaptable to different screen sizes and orientations, changes that appear to be laying some of the groundwork for its expected folding iPhone. Safari Safari will automatically group tabs into topics, making related pages easier to find. A new Notify Me feature will monitor webpages and alert you to changes such as price drops or products coming back into stock. Apple is also adding Describe an Extension, which lets users create custom Safari extensions simply by explaining what they want the extension to do. Apple Photos Photos gains significantly more powerful AI editing tools . Spatial Reframing/Reframe can alter the composition and perspective of an existing photo, while Extend generates new image content beyond the original frame when straightening a horizon or changing the aspect ratio. Apple Clean Up has also been improved, with Fast and High Quality modes for removing unwanted objects. High Quality mode can produce considerably more natural results, although more ambitious edits can still introduce distortions or invented details. Photos also adds new categories and the ability to save a frame from a video as a full-resolution photo. The resulting HEIF or JPG retains the video’s original resolution, date and location metadata rather than simply creating a screenshot. Camera Apple is developing a customizable Camera interface, although it has not appeared consistently throughout the iOS 27 beta cycle. It could arrive in a later iOS 27 update . Apple is also reportedly developing Apple Reference Image , an authentication system designed to prove that a photo or video was genuinely captured on an iPhone and has not subsequently been manipulated. The feature would use additional metadata and Apple’s Private Cloud Compute to authenticate an image and assign it a unique ID. Its usefulness may be greatest for journalists, insurers and investigators rather than as a general solution to AI-generated imagery, particularly because authentication would be optional and social networks frequently remove metadata. Messages Foundry Messages gets several useful improvements. You can also decide what the microphone button beside the text field does . Under Settings > Apps > Messages > Show in Text Field, it can be set to Record Audio, Start Dictation or None. Disabling it does not remove either feature: dictation remains available from the keyboard and audio messages remain in the + menu. Voice-message playback controls are easier to access, while Apple Intelligence can suggest actions based on a conversation, such as creating a reminder, making a note or finding relevant photos. Messages will also gain smarter suggested replies that can better reflect the user’s writing style. Drawing Foundry A new dedicated Drawing app replaces the old hidden handwriting interface. Accessible from the + menu, it uses the familiar pens, colours and drawing controls found in Notes and Markup, with finished drawings sent as images. Mail Mail gains more context-aware smart replies, including responses that can better match the user’s usual writing style. Apple Intelligence can also surface information from Mail elsewhere in iOS. For example, the Phone app could retrieve a flight confirmation number from an email when you call an airline. Phone A new Call Context feature can surface information that may be useful when calling a business. Apple says the information is selected according to who you are calling rather than by listening to the conversation. For example, calling an airline could cause iOS to surface the relevant flight confirmation from Mail. Birthday reminders can also appear when calling contacts whose birthdays are stored on the iPhone. FaceTime FaceTime gains Dual Capture, allowing the front and rear cameras to be used at the same time during a call. Passwords Passwords in iOS 27 will fix things for you. Apple The Passwords app will continue to warn about weak, reused and compromised credentials, but iOS 27 goes a step further by offering to fix some of them automatically. Using Apple Intelligence, Passwords can visit supported websites, change a vulnerable password and save the replacement credentials. See: Apple got rid of my biggest password headache . The usefulness of the feature will depend on how widely websites are supported and how well it handles obstacles such as two-factor authentication and unusual account-management interfaces. Shortcuts Shortcuts gains Describe a Shortcut, allowing users to create automations simply by explaining what they want to happen. Apple Intelligence will interpret the request and assemble the appropriate actions across supported apps, potentially making Shortcuts significantly easier to use for people unfamiliar with building automations manually. Calendar Calendar can create or modify events from natural-language instructions. Apple says the app can recognise contacts, locations, dates and other event details as users type, reducing the amount of information that needs to be entered manually. Image Playground Image Playground is becoming considerably more powerful. Apple says it can create photorealistic images and lets users modify generated pictures simply by describing the changes they want. Individual objects can also be selected, resized or repositioned. AI-generated images will include a SynthID watermark identifying them as synthetic content. Wallet Wallet can create custom passes from QR codes. Users can add their own fields and information to the pass, and passes automatically sync to Apple Watch. Home app Apple Intelligence comes to the Home app for compatible HomeKit Secure Video cameras. It can group related camera notifications, describe recorded video and highlight clips that appear particularly noteworthy. Maps Apple Maps improves Flyover using higher-quality aerial imagery and Visual Intelligence models. Apple says this produces sharper architectural detail and more realistic rendering of elements such as individual trees. Podcasts Video podcasts become easier to use, with improved controls for switching between watching a podcast and simply listening to it. Fitness Workout summaries have been redesigned to make them easier to share. Users can also hide completed Fitness+ workouts. iOS 27 changes beyond the iPhone CarPlay CarPlay gains an audio scrubber, giving drivers and passengers more direct control when moving through audio tracks and other content. AirPods iOS 27 introduces several new AirPods features . A new Custom EQ lets users independently adjust bass, mids and treble using a simple three-band equalizer under Settings > AirPods > Audio and Routing > Equalizer > Custom. Compatible AirPods also gain improved Precision Finding through Find My, making individual earbuds easier to locate. Some features require both iOS 27 and compatible AirPods firmware. Read How to tune your AirPods with a custom EQ in iOS 27 . Other changes coming with iOS 27 It’s not only individual apps that will see changes. Home Screen and landscape mode Apple is making iOS significantly more flexible when dealing with different screen orientations and sizes. More Apple apps now work properly in landscape, including Health, Home, Music, Weather and Watch. Dynamic Island and Live Activities can also adapt to landscape orientation. The Home Screen additionally supports extra-large widgets. These changes could simply improve iPhone usability, but they also appear well suited to Apple’s expected folding iPhone, which is likely to have an unusual, wider aspect ratio. Evidence within Apple’s software also includes new foldState and angleDegrees variables that could allow apps to respond to whether a device is folded and at what angle. iPhone Mirroring in macOS 27 has similarly become freely resizable, with Apple apps dynamically rearranging their interfaces as the window changes shape. Liquid Glass refinements Apple Apple says Liquid Glass has been refined for better readability, more uniform refraction and improved contrast. A new slider lets users adjust the look from ultraclear to fully tinted, while updated icons, toolbars, sidebars and window shapes add polish. Ringtones, alarms and alert volume iOS 27 finally separates several sound-volume controls . Instead of one combined Ringtone and Alerts slider, users can independently adjust: Ringtones Alarms and timers Alerts and system sounds The change is optional. Under Settings > Sounds & Haptics, turning off Match Ringtone Volume reveals separate controls. Media and call volume continue to work independently as before. Keyboard iOS 27 introduces a new quick-paste control above the keyboard. It lets you paste recently copied text, images or screenshots without having to long-press inside a text field, making everyday copy-and-paste considerably faster. Apple has also made the Liquid Glass keyboard design more consistent across apps. Privacy and Find My iOS 27 introduces the ability to temporarily pause Find My location sharing without notifying the person with whom the location is normally shared. Recovery and troubleshooting Apple is also expanding the iPhone’s recovery interface, giving users more options for diagnosing problems and recovering an iPhone without immediately connecting it to another device. System changes and how iOS 27 will make your iPhone faster Alongside the headline AI features, Apple says iOS 27 includes a wide range of under-the-hood improvements designed to make iPhones faster , smoother and more efficient. Apple says apps can launch up to 30% faster, newly taken photos can appear in the Photos library up to 70% faster, and AirDrop transfers can be up to 80% quicker. External drive transfers should also improve, while updates to network performance and the system-wide search index are designed to make connectivity and finding information faster. The company has also reworked core technologies including CPU scheduling, display performance and processing efficiency. These changes should benefit older iPhones in particular, with Apple promising smoother performance and more efficient battery use on devices as old as the iPhone 11 and second-generation iPhone SE. Our testing of the iOS 27 beta supports those claims. On an iPhone 11 Pro Max, Camera launch time fell from 0.98 seconds in iOS 26 to 0.65 seconds in iOS 27, while Maps improved from 3.01 seconds to 1.36 seconds. Everyday use also feels smoother, with more fluid animations, unlocking, Control Center and app transitions. The phone ran cooler during testing too, which could point to improved system efficiency and potentially better battery performance. More broadly, iOS 27 appears focused on refinement rather than simply adding new features. Apple says it has addressed dozens of common user frustrations, while changes such as more adjustable Liquid Glass effects are intended to improve readability and general usability. That focus should make iOS 27 particularly worthwhile for owners of older iPhones, even on models that do not support Siri AI. Those devices still gain performance improvements alongside features such as clipboard tools for the keyboard, independent alarm and timer volume controls, custom Wallet passes, Photos changes, larger widgets and Liquid Glass refinements. Child safety and parental controls Apple There are lots of improvements coming to parental controls, including new time allowances for entertainments, games, and social media, and new schedule tools for different times of day or days of the week. This includes new features like an expansion of the existing “ask to buy” feature for apps to websites. Before a child can view a new website, they’ll have to ask for permission. Ask to Browse : Ask to Browse will expand the current Ask to Buy fetaure to the web. Apple says children will need to request permission before visiting new websites, and parents can review requests in Messages before approving. Communication Safety : Communication Safety will continue to help protect children from viewing or sharing nudity in Messages, FaceTime and other apps. Apple says it will also intervene before children see gore or violent content in shared images and videos. Time Allowances and schedules : Parents will be able to set Time Allowances across categories such as Entertainment, Games and Social Media. Recommendations are based on a child’s age combined with guidance from clinical and child development experts. Schedules let parents choose which apps are available at different times or on different days. Redesigned Screen Time : Screen Time will get a redesigned interface with an at-a-glance view of average device usage and most-used apps. Apple says parents can quickly limit or extend access in the moment. Child accounts and family safety : Apple says child accounts remain central to age-appropriate protections. Parents can manage app access, web access, communication permissions and Screen Time settings. Apple says it is working with the American Academy of Pediatrics to adapt its Family Media Plan. Accessibility changes coming in iOS 27 Accessibility features will be smarter and more intuitive in iOS 27: VoiceOver will get richer image descriptions and better understanding of onscreen content. Live Recognition will let users press the Action button to ask questions about their surroundings and receive detailed responses. Voice Control will become more intuitive, allowing users to describe onscreen buttons and controls rather than remembering exact labels or numbers. Accessibility Reader will be able to handle more complex source material and provide summaries and translation. iOS 27 compatibility iPhone 11 is supported by iOS 27. Roman Loyola/IDG According to Apple, iOS 27 supports iPhones back to the iPhone 11 and second-generation iPhone SE, although some Apple Intelligence and Siri AI features require newer hardware. Support for iOS 27 does not mean every device gets every feature. Apple Intelligence requires an iPhone 15 Pro or iPhone 16 or later, while the most advanced on-device AI models require an iPhone 17 Pro or iPhone Air. On iPad, Apple Intelligence requires an M1-class model or the A17 Pro iPad mini, while the newest on-device models require an M4 iPad with at least 12GB of RAM. There had been speculation that the iPhone 11 series and iPhone SE 2 would miss out on iOS 27 after leaker Instant Digital claimed on Weibo that the 2019 iPhone 11, 11 Pro and 11 Pro Max, along with the 2020 iPhone SE 2, would no longer be supported. That prediction proved incorrect, giving those models at least one more year of software support. However, the iPhone 11 generation is nearing the end of its support life. As we explain in our guide to how long Apple supports iPhones , the iPhone 11 Pro and 11 Pro Max have already been added to Apple’s Vintage iPhone list . The iOS 27 compatibility list is: iPhone 17e (launched in 2026 ) iPhone 17 , 17 Pro / 17 Pro Max (launched in 2025 ) iPhone Air (launched in 2025 ) iPhone 16e (launched in 2025 ) iPhone 16 / 16 Plus and iPhone 16 Pro / 16 Pro Max (launched in 2024 ) iPhone 15 / 15 Plus and iPhone 15 Pro / 15 Pro Max (launched in 2023 ) iPhone 14 / 14 Plus / 14 Pro / 14 Pro Max (launched in 2022 ) iPhone SE 3 (launched in 2022 ) iPhone 13 / 13 mini / 13 Pro / 13 Pro Max (launched in 2021 ) iPhone 12 / 12 mini / 12 Pro / 12 Pro Max (launched in 2020 ) iPhone SE 2 (launched in 2020 ) iPhone 11 / 11 Pro / 11 Pro Max (launched in 2019 ) The main dividing line for Apple Intelligence remains the iPhone 15 Pro generation: the standard iPhone 15 and all older models can run iOS 27, but they do not support Apple Intelligence. FAQ 1. When is iOS 27 coming out? Apple hasn’t confirmed exactly when iOS 27 will be available to install, but it usually launches to the general public in September, or at the latest October. Once iOS 27 launches Apple will likely continue beta development to test new features that weren’t available at launch. 2. Should I install the iOS 27 beta? Installing a beta lets you test new features ahead of release, so you may be keen to install the beta on your iPhone, but before you do beware of the risks. For most users, the recommendation is simple: don’t install the beta. Pre-release software can be unstable. Bugs, performance issues, and app incompatibility are common as Apple uses the beta period to identify and fix problems before the final version launches. If, despite our warnings, you’re still eager to try the new features, be sure to make a backup of all important information, passwords, and so on. If you want to uninstall the iOS 27 beta read: How to remove an iOS beta from your iPhone. 3. Which iPhones get iOS 27? The iPhone 11 and iPhone SE 2 and newer get iOS 27. However, the new Siri voices feature requires iPhone Air, iPhone 17 Pro or newer.
paragraphs: Apple has officially unveiled the new features coming to compatible iPhones running iOS 27 later this year, introducing major Apple Intelligence upgrades, changes to Siri, parental controls enhancements and improvements across core iPhone apps.

iOS 27 is currently available as a beta test version for developers and public testers. The software has been going through several months of testing before its full public release – which is likely to happen in the next few weeks. Apple typically launches new versions of iOS in September, often around the second week – making Monday, September 14 a likely release date based on past patterns.
iOS 27 will be supported on every iPhone all the way back to iPhone 11 and iPhone SE 2, though some Apple Intelligence and Siri related features will only be available on newer iPhones.

This hub contains everything Apple has confirmed will be coming in iOS 27 when it launches, including new features, compatible iPhones, beta release information, Apple Intelligence updates and what’s new for Siri.
iOS 27 has been in beta since it was unveiled at WWDC in June, but the official version of iOS 27 will not be available to install on compatible iPhones until later in 2026.

Apple has confirmed that the iPhone launch event will take place on September 9, so we anticipate that iOS 27 will be available to download on Monday, September 14, as the iOS download usually closely follows Apple’s September event.

macOS 27: Final release to support Rosetta — Intel-only apps will no longer run on Mac computers with Apple silicon after this update.

article.title: Agentic security: Detection and response at machine speed
article.summary: After talking with enterprise security leaders over the past year, one thing has become clear: the rise of autonomous AI agents is the most significant shift in security posture since the move to cloud. Organizations across every industry are adopting AI agents that authenticate on behalf of users, execute multistep workflows, and make decisions across infrastructure, often without waiting for human approval.

sections.heading: Context: what is changing
sections.body: After talking with enterprise security leaders over the past year, one thing has become clear: the rise of autonomous AI agents is the most significant shift in security posture since the move to cloud. Organizations across every industry are adopting AI agents that authenticate on behalf of users, execute multistep workflows, and make decisions across infrastructure, often without waiting for human approval. Security operations need to keep pace.

sections.heading: Where the sources line up
sections.body: At Amazon Web Services (AWS) , we believe security should evolve ahead of AI adoption, not behind it. That belief drove our team to collaborate with the SANS Institute on a new chapter in the 2026 Cloud Security Exchange eBook , where we lay out a practical framework for securing agentic workloads at enterprise scale.

sections.heading: Practical impact for readers
sections.body: Traditional security was built for deterministic systems with predictable inputs and outputs. Agentic workloads break those assumptions. The same prompt can produce a compliant response on one request and a policy-violating response on the next. Agents adapt their behavior over time as they interact with users, data, and tools and operate with genuine autonomy: connecting to APIs, chaining actions together, and making independent decisions.

sections.heading: Who should pay attention now

draft_context.source_title: Agentic security: Detection and response at machine speed
draft_context.description: After talking with enterprise security leaders over the past year, one thing has become clear: the rise of autonomous AI agents is the most significant shift in security posture since the move to cloud. Organizations across every industry are adopting AI agents that authenticate on behalf of users, execute multistep workflows, and make decisions across infrastructure, often without waiting for human approval. Security operations need to keep pace. At Amazon Web Services (AWS) , we believe security should evolve ahead of AI adoption, not behind it. That belief drove our team to collaborate with the SANS Institute on a new chapter in the 2026 Cloud Security Exchange eBook , where we lay out a practical framework for securing agentic workloads at enterprise scale. The challenge: Threats now move at machine speed Traditional security was built for deterministic systems with predictable inputs and outputs. Agentic workloads break those assumptions. The same prompt can produce a compliant response on one request and a policy-violating response on the next. Agents adapt their behavior over time as they interact with users, data, and tools and operate with genuine autonomy: connecting to APIs, chaining actions together, and making independent decisions. These properties mean that security controls designed for one-time assessments no longer suffice. Detection and response need to operate continuously and at machine speed. What makes this urgent is the gap between adoption velocity and security maturity. Although 80% of organizations have adopted AI, only 10% govern it. Agents are being built by an expanding population of developers—including those using low-code tools—creating governance challenges that existing security programs must be extended to address. Extending what already works The good news, agentic security isn’t a blank slate. It builds on the same principles security teams already apply: identity governance, least privilege, defense in depth, and backup and recovery. What changes is how those principles are implemented when workloads are autonomous and probabilistic. In our eBook chapter, we cover four foundational areas: Agent identity and governance: Every agent needs its own identity with temporary, scoped credentials rather than persistent, broad access. This extends zero trust principles to AI agents, where every request is authenticated and authorized independently, and every action has a traceable authorization chain. When a single agent combines access to sensitive data, the ability to communicate externally, and exposure to untrusted content, the risk profile changes significantly. Design patterns that prevent any single component from combining all three reduce that risk substantially. Evolving detection for agentic workloads: Static, rule-based detection designed for human activity patterns can’t keep up with agent behavior. Organizations need continuous behavioral monitoring, living baselines that adapt as agents evolve, and instrumented observation that surfaces anomalies in real time. Amazon GuardDuty delivers this today, analyzing security signals continuously to detect threats as they emerge. Response that balances speed with precision: When threats move at machine speed, response must be automated and tiered: some agent behaviors should be contained immediately, others require human judgment. The response framework we outline distinguishes between actions that can be automated safely and those that need escalation. From single agents to multiagent ecosystems: Agents are already composing into teams, delegating subtasks, negotiating access, and coordinating across organizational boundaries. Each stage of this evolution inherits every security requirement that came before it, meaning organizations securing today’s basic chat agents are already laying the foundation for tomorrow’s multiagent ecosystems. Security as an enabler of agentic AI adoption The security leaders I speak with aren’t asking whether to adopt AI agents. They’re asking how to adopt them responsibly, at speed, and without slowing down the business. AWS approaches this challenge by building security into the platform at every layer. Agentic AI built on AWS inherits nearly two decades of experience securing mission-critical workloads. Amazon GuardDuty , Amazon Inspector , and AWS Security Hub work together to provide continuous threat detection, vulnerability management, and unified security operations, all adapting to the unique characteristics of agentic workloads. This isn’t about building new security from scratch. It’s about extending the security foundations your teams already trust into an environment where AI operates with increasing autonomy. Read the full framework Our chapter in the 2026 Cloud Security Exchange eBook goes deeper on each of these areas, with specific architectural patterns, implementation guidance, and frameworks for security teams at every stage of agentic AI maturity, whether you’re evaluating, piloting, or operating at scale. Read the 2026 Cloud Security Exchange eBook: Agentic Security: Detection and Response at Machine Speed You can learn more about AWS security services at AWS Cloud Security , or explore our AI Security Framework for a comprehensive view of how AWS secures AI workloads with the right controls, at the right layers, at the right phases. If you have feedback about this post, submit comments in the Comments section below. Gee Rittenhouse Gee is the Vice President of Agentic Security at AWS. He holds a PhD from MIT and brings extensive leadership experience across enterprise security and cloud. He previously served as CEO of Skyhigh Security and Senior Vice President and General Manager of Cisco’s Security Business Group, where he was responsible for Cisco’s worldwide cybersecurity business.

paragraphs: The demonstration ran in coordination with the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group, under the sponsorship of the US Navy's Fleet Experimentation Program, and the fire control ran through the Navy's Adjunct Remote Engagement System (ARES), which Lockheed describes as "a remotely operated combat system."
The exercise, which could be seen as a fully autonomous play based on earlier coverage, involved relaying remote targeting information to the Saildrone Surveyor, which it acted on successfully.

This isn't the first time a USV has launched a missile; The USV Ranger fired an SM-6 from a containerized four-cell launcher in September 2021 under the Ghost Fleet Overlord program, and Ukraine has since moved the concept from test range to combat, with its Magura-series drone boats using adapted R-73 air-to-air missiles to shoot down Russian helicopters and, as per claims, potentially an Su-30 fighter.

Its weapon choice says more about the platform's intended target; the JAGM is the successor to the Hellfire missile, a 50kg weapon with an 18km effective targeting radius. This makes it not a ship-killer, but a platform that overwhelmingly targets smaller, faster aerial and naval targets such as one-way drones and small boats.

Arming what is effectively a relatively expendable platform with the same could make it considerably more lethal at a fraction of the cost of an alternate warship.

At the same time, the Surveyor's passive electronic warfare sensor, as demonstrated during the same RIMPAC outing, allows it to detect, classify, and identify threats in conjunction with an MH-60 helicopter, essentially doubling down as a support platform for larger threats.

Recently, security researchers from Forescout set off on a simple mission - to understand if crooks can use AI to target the ever-increasing population of exposed industrial devices. The short answer is “yes, but it’s not yet worth the trouble”. In their mission, they launched an experiment - to port a remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability from one PLC to another. These devices were built on closed-source software and thus were not that easy to manipulate, yet the experiment was a success. Yes, but... Not only did they manage to trigger a Denial of Service (DoS) state that crashed the device but ended up with a working RCE capable of executing attacker-supplied ARM shellcode. It is indeed a worrying development, but one that comes with a huge “but”: “It required significant researcher input. The final RCE development stage consumed more than $500 in API usage. An attempt to extend the exploit beyond the initial RCE ultimately bricked the PLC,” the researchers said in the report. “These limitations taught us valuable lessons about AI-assisted exploitation in OT. It can be done, but it’s not as easy as it sounds. For now, the difficulty, cost, and specialist expertise required are likely to make this kind of attack less attractive than easier alternatives.” In other words, cybercriminals still have easier avenues to explore, and as long as that is the case, OT is relatively safe. What the report, unfortunately, does not discuss, is nation-state attackers with significant resources. For such attackers, industrial devices are a prime target, and spending $500+ in API usage is a drop in a bucket. We’ve already seen it back in 2025 when Sandworm struck Poland’s electricity suppliers . ]]>
paragraphs: Recently, security researchers from Forescout set off on a simple mission - to understand if crooks can use AI to target the ever-increasing population of exposed industrial devices. The short answer is “yes, but it’s not yet worth the trouble”.

In their mission, they launched an experiment - to port a remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability from one PLC to another. These devices were built on closed-source software and thus were not that easy to manipulate, yet the experiment was a success.
Not only did they manage to trigger a Denial of Service (DoS) state that crashed the device but ended up with a working RCE capable of executing attacker-supplied ARM shellcode.

Hackers are using “evolved” capabilities in AI-generated malware to hit US critical infrastructure Experts explain why OpenAI's 'mind-blowing' cyberattack should worry us all Autonomous AI worms mark a new era of adaptive cyberattacks “It required significant researcher input. The final RCE development stage consumed more than $500 in API usage. An attempt to extend the exploit beyond the initial RCE ultimately bricked the PLC,” the researchers said in the report.

“These limitations taught us valuable lessons about AI-assisted exploitation in OT. It can be done, but it’s not as easy as it sounds. For now, the difficulty, cost, and specialist expertise required are likely to make this kind of attack less attractive than easier alternatives.”

draft_context.source_title: Call of Duty: Warzone's Xbox One and PS4 shut down is approaching — here's what's happening and when you have to stop playing
draft_context.description: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is fast approaching now that the traditional yearly beta test is out of the way. Included for the first time this year was a look at the next iteration of Call of Duty: Warzone, the free-to-play battle royale that ties in with a current year's game. It's bittersweet for folks still on an Xbox One or a PS4, though, because they weren't able to try out the new Zodiac map, and they're never going to, either. Modern Warfare 4 will be the first Call of Duty title to drop support for Xbox One and PS4 , and along with it, Warzone. The announcement was made back in June, but for now, the game is still playable. That's going to change fairly soon, though. Here's what's already happened, what's going to happen, and crucially, when we think the final shutdown will happen. Why is Call of Duty: Warzone on Xbox One and PS4 being shut down? Once the Black Ops 7 integration is over, Warzone is no more on last-gen consoles. (Image credit: Windows Central) The simple answer is that Warzone is shutting down on Xbox One and PS4 because Modern Warfare 4 will not be on those platforms. Despite Warzone being free-to-play without any requirement to own the latest Call of Duty game, crucially, it integrates with each year's new game. As Modern Warfare 4 will be taking over from Black Ops 7, and it won't be supported on the last-gen consoles, Warzone will no longer be playable. When do we think Call of Duty: Warzone is shutting down on Xbox One and PS4? Both the PlayStation 4 and Xbox One family of consoles are affected. (Image credit: Windows Central) The official documentation states : "Call of Duty: Warzone on PlayStation 4 and XBOX One will be available to play through the end of Season 06 for Call of Duty: Black Ops 7." Activision hasn't given an exact date yet , but we can make an educated guess based on how the new games have rolled out in previous years. Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 will release on Friday, October 23, 2026 . The assumption may be that this is when the Warzone shutdown will happen, but it's not that straightforward. Traditionally, the Warzone integration doesn't go live when the new game launches. It follows on when Season 1 of said new game begins. In the case of Black Ops 6 and Black Ops 7, Season 1 began 20 days post-launch of the game, and this is when Warzone was updated with the new game's integration. In the case of Modern Warfare III, it was actually almost a week longer. We expect Season 06 to begin on September 17 , given it's both a Thursday and the date the Season 05 battle pass expires. Unlike the jump from Black Ops 6 to Black Ops 7, where there was a month without a seasonal update, it looks like this year's transition will leave us with content right to the very end. This year isn't an in-house transition like the past two Treyarch releases. Given how long the seasons in Black Ops 7 usually are, we could be looking at Season 06 ending after Modern Warfare 4 launches. This means Xbox One and PS4 players could have until around November 12 to keep playing Warzone. But we'll know for sure once Season 06 begins when we can expect it to end. But it wouldn't be crazy to assume that Black Ops 7, the Season 06 content, Battle Pass, and Warzone that is linked to it all could remain live this long. It would be about 20 days after the Modern Warfare 4 launch, too. Can I still get Call of Duty: Warzone on Xbox One and PS4? You can still get Warzone if you played it before, but you can't buy anything. (Image credit: Windows Central) For now, you can only play Warzone on Xbox One or PS4 if you have previously added it to your library. No new downloads are being offered on either console, but if you're a past player, you can still reinstall it and play until the shutdown date. The store is also disabled now, despite showing up in the launcher. You're unable to spend anymore money or redeem COD Points. What happens to all the stuff I've bought in Call of Duty: Warzone on Xbox One and PS4? The store is no longer accessible from Warzone on the Xbox One and PS4. (Image credit: Windows Central) The in-game store has been closed for a while now, preventing players from spending real money via the Xbox One and PS4 versions. But your purchases aren't disappearing. Because you have an Activision ID in order to play, all those purchases are tied to your account. As such, if you log in on another platform at any time, you'll have everything there waiting for you. I don't have an Xbox Series X|S, PS5, or gaming PC, so how can I keep playing Call of Duty: Warzone If you don't have hardware to keep playing natively, the cloud can help. (Image credit: Windows Central) If you don't have more current hardware to move to or don't want to upgrade, you're all but out of options. You do, however, have the ability to play Warzone via the cloud, either through Xbox Cloud Gaming or NVIDIA GeForce Now. The former, you can use on your Xbox One. Is it the same experience? Not totally. The visuals and frame rate will certainly be an upgrade (especially on GeForce Now) but you do have to consider that you will have some additional latency concerns. The game will be playing on a piece of hardware that's in someone else's building. While server latency in the game won't be too bad, you then have to stream the game to your own device. Cloud gaming has come a long way, though, and unless you're the absolute most competitive player, it might well be good enough. The downside is that you're going to have to pay, even though NVIDIA does have a free tier. This one is limited to an hour's play, and you have no priority access, so if the servers are full, you'll be in a longer queue. And who wants to be chucked out in the final circle? Likewise, you can't play Warzone via the cloud for free with Xbox Cloud Gaming, either. Ultimate gets you the best quality stream, but you can play via the cheaper tiers, too. So, that's where we're at. While Warzone has indeed been playable on Xbox One, it's hardly been the best experience. The Xbox One X still does OK, but being attached to the Xbox One generation it has to say goodbye, too. But there's still probably a couple of months at least left to play from the time of writing this, so enjoy. Join us on Reddit at r/WindowsCentral to share your insights and discuss our latest news, reviews, and more. ]]>

article.title: What is a cold wallet and how does it work?
article.summary: Z1b/Getty Images Cryptocurrency security has always been a matter of great debate, especially as high-profile trading platforms have lost customer assets through security breaches over the years. Online communities also commonly chant the mantra of "not your keys, not your coins." Self-custody can be the best way to insulate yourself from third-party risk, but you have to take sole responsibility for securing your holdings.

sections.heading: Context: what is changing
sections.body: Z1b/Getty Images Cryptocurrency security has always been a matter of great debate, especially as high-profile trading platforms have lost customer assets through security breaches over the years. Online communities also commonly chant the mantra of "not your keys, not your coins." Self-custody can be the best way to insulate yourself from third-party risk, but you have to take sole responsibility for securing your holdings. This is why cold wallets have become an attractive option, as they keep your cryptocurrency balance as safe as possible and entirely within your control.

sections.heading: Where the sources line up
sections.body: While you can achieve self-custody with a simple wallet app on your phone or computer, a cold wallet is arguably the most secure option. So how do these cold wallets work, what makes them secure and what should you keep in mind before picking one?

sections.heading: Practical impact for readers
sections.body: There is one significant difference between hot and cold wallets. A hot wallet lives on a device that can be connected to the internet, while a cold wallet stays offline. The cold wallet's isolation keeps your private keys away from malicious attackers, which in turn, improves the overall security of any cryptocurrency you own.

sections.heading: Who should pay attention now
sections.body: But before getting too deep into why hot and cold wallets matter, it's worth exploring what a cryptocurrency wallet does. Despite their name, cryptocurrency wallets don't actually hold any of your funds within them. Instead, it's best to think of any cryptocurrency you own as a balance recorded on a blockchain network, like Bitcoin or Ethereum. Your wallet simply holds the cryptographic keys necessary to prove ownership over your balance, similar to an online bank account you'd.

sections.heading: What to watch next
sections.body: A paper wallet is the most basic kind of cryptocurrency, as it's just a physical piece of paper. It includes the private keys that allow you to access your cryptocurrency on the blockchain, commonly represented as a list of 12 or 24 words. However, you must still use an app or program to authorize transactions through a process called signing.

paragraphs: Z1b/Getty Images Cryptocurrency security has always been a matter of great debate, especially as high-profile trading platforms have lost customer assets through security breaches over the years. Online communities also commonly chant the mantra of "not your keys, not your coins." Self-custody can be the best way to insulate yourself from third-party risk, but you have to take sole responsibility for securing your holdings. This is why cold wallets have become an attractive option, as they keep your cryptocurrency balance as safe as possible and entirely within your control.

While you can achieve self-custody with a simple wallet app on your phone or computer, a cold wallet is arguably the most secure option. So how do these cold wallets work, what makes them secure and what should you keep in mind before picking one?

There is one significant difference between hot and cold wallets. A hot wallet lives on a device that can be connected to the internet, while a cold wallet stays offline. The cold wallet's isolation keeps your private keys away from malicious attackers, which in turn, improves the overall security of any cryptocurrency you own.

But before getting too deep into why hot and cold wallets matter, it's worth exploring what a cryptocurrency wallet does. Despite their name, cryptocurrency wallets don't actually hold any of your funds within them. Instead, it's best to think of any cryptocurrency you own as a balance recorded on a blockchain network, like Bitcoin or Ethereum. Your wallet simply holds the cryptographic keys necessary to prove ownership over your balance, similar to an online bank account you'd

A paper wallet is the most basic kind of cryptocurrency, as it's just a physical piece of paper. It includes the private keys that allow you to access your cryptocurrency on the blockchain, commonly represented as a list of 12 or 24 words. However, you must still use an app or program to authorize transactions through a process called signing.

Many modern wallets are primarily designed around convenience. Software wallets like smartphone or desktop apps offer the most assistance, allowing you to sign transactions from anywhere. Hardware wallets, on the other hand, keep your private keys isolated on a dedicated device. You'll still use an app to initiate transactions, but the signing process takes place entirely on the dedicated hardware. This is why you typically need to connect a hardware wallet to your phone or computer via USB, Bluetooth or NFC.

draft_context.source_title: With Gemini 3.8 Flash, Google reminds everyone it's still in the race
draft_context.description: Google on Wednesday announced the release of Gemini 3.8 Flash in an attempt to reclaim its reputation as a top-tier model maker in the process. The company's commitment to the frontier model race has been in doubt since at least early August when Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis stepped down to become chairman of the AI research biz and Koray Kavukcuoglu took over leadership under a less exalted title, SVP. Google CEO Sundar Pichai's reassurances weren't particularly convincing in light of the company's failure to release Gemini 3.5 Pro in June as promised. Nor were they helped by the modest benchmark metrics of Gemini 3.5 Flash, which, while speedy and cost-efficient, have been overshadowed in terms of intelligence scores by open-weight models from Chinese AI companies over the past few months. But Google has been iterating rapidly. Gemini 3.8 Flash is its fourth Flash model in as many months and it has improved enough to be considered alongside the highest scoring models in terms of intelligence while also being performant and relatively affordable – at least until its introductory price ($0.75/M input tokens, $3.75/M output tokens) doubles in the new year. "Gemini 3.8 Flash delivers substantial gains from 3.7 Flash, often approaching the performance of higher-cost frontier models," said Tulsee Doshi, Google senior director of product management, and Raluca Ada Popa, Gemini Security Lead at Google DeepMind, in a blog post. "On DeepSWE v1.1 (Long-Horizon Software Engineering) 3.8 Flash outperforms most larger frontier models in autonomously solving complex engineering problems end to end, only at a fraction of the cost." Gemini 3.8 Flash, set to high reasoning, scores 59 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, an increase of three points from its predecessor. That puts it level with GPT-5.6 Sol (extra high, 59) and Grok 4.6 (medium, 59). From there, current intelligence rankings, based on nine benchmarks, are: GLM-5.3 (max, 60), Kimi K3 (max, 60), Grok 4.6 (high, 61), GPT-5.6 Sol (max, 61), Claude Opus 5 (max, 63), and Claude Fable 5.1 (max, 66). At $0.58 per Intelligence Index task, Gemini 3.8 Flash is "the cheapest model at its level of intelligence," according to Artificial Analysis. As a point of comparison, Anthropic's latest general usage flagship model, Fable 5.1, costs about 6x more – $3.76 per Intelligence Index task. Gemini 3.8 Flash costs about 40 percent more per task than its similarly priced predecessor because it tends to output more tokens and to execute more turns when acting as an agent. "3.8 Flash works harder," explain Doshi and Popa. "On complex tasks, it exhibits greater diligence – executing extra reasoning steps, and calling tools iteratively. At times, the model might use more tokens to maximize performance, especially at higher effort levels." The two Googlers also note that Gemini 3.8 Flash shows improvements in benchmarks relevant to enterprise knowledge work, like Vals Finance Agent V2, Harvey's Legal Agent Benchmark, and HLE-Verified. Gemini 3.8 Flash is available for developers through Google Antigravity, the Gemini API in Google AI Studio and Android Studio, and interface design service Stitch. Enterprises can use Gemini Enterprise. Consumers with Google AI Pro and Ultra subscriptions can access the model via the Gemini app, AI Mode in Google Search, and Gemini in Google Sheets. Google has also launched the Fairwind Program to provide governments, critical infrastructure organizations, and software maintainers with access to Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber, a version of the model tuned for software vulnerability hunting and remediation. ®

article.title: Google ra Gemini 3.8 Flash, vẫn chưa thấy bản Pro đâu
article.summary: Ngày 2/9, Google ra mắt Gemini 3.8 Flash và biến thể an ninh mạng Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber, chỉ một ngày sau khi Anthropic tung Claude Fable 5.1 và Mythos 5.1. Nhưng trong khi Anthropic nâng cấp thẳng vào dòng model mạnh nhất của mình, Google lại tiếp tục đưa ra một bản Flash, phân khúc tầm trung giá rẻ, thay vì Gemini 3.5 Pro, model đầu bảng mà giới công nghệ chờ đợi suốt nhiều tháng qua.

sections.body: Đây đã là bản Flash thứ ba Google ra mắt chỉ trong 6 tuần, sau Gemini 3.6 Flash ngày 21/7 và Gemini 3.7 Flash ngày 13/8. Trong khi đó, Gemini 3.5 Pro, model đầu bảng thực sự của hãng, vẫn chưa có ngày ra mắt cụ thể, dù CEO Sundar Pichai từng nói hồi tháng 7 rằng model đang được thử nghiệm cùng đối tác. Đầu tháng 8, Google cũng thay nhân sự cấp cao tại DeepMind: Demis Hassabis rời vị trí điều hành hàng ngày để giữ vai trò Chủ tịch, còn Koray Kavukcuoglu, cựu Giám đốc công nghệ DeepMind, tiếp quản việc phát triển Gemini và báo cáo trực tiếp cho Sundar Pichai.

sections.heading: Ai nên chú ý lúc này
sections.body: Về giá, Gemini 3.8 Flash giữ nguyên mức giới thiệu của bản 3.7 Flash: 0,75 USD cho mỗi triệu token đầu vào và 3,75 USD cho mỗi triệu token đầu ra, tương đương khoảng 19.700 đồng và 98.600 đồng, áp dụng đến hết năm 2026. Từ 1/1/2027, giá tăng lên 1,50 USD và 7,50 USD, tương đương khoảng 39.400 đồng và 197.000 đồng.

sections.heading: Điều cần theo dõi tiếp
sections.body: Google cho biết Gemini 3.8 Flash vượt phần lớn model đầu bảng lớn hơn trên DeepSWE v1.1, benchmark đo khả năng tự giải quyết các bài toán kỹ thuật phần mềm dài hơi, dù chi phí thấp hơn nhiều. Model cũng dẫn trước cả Gemini 3.7 Flash lẫn các model đầu bảng khác trên hai benchmark chuyên ngành Vals Finance Agent V2 và Harvey Legal Agent Benchmark, đồng thời đạt 54,9% trên HLE-Verified, bài kiểm tra suy luận nhiều bước trải rộng các lĩnh vực khoa học, nhân văn và chuyên môn. Cách model đạt điểm cao là "làm việc chăm hơn": tự thêm bước suy luận, gọi công cụ nhiều lần hơn, có thể tốn nhiều token hơn khi đặt mức effort cao. Google khuyên hạ effort nếu ưu tiên tiết kiệm chi phí, hoặc tiếp tục dùng Gemini 3.7 Flash cho các tác vụ cần hiệu quả token.

sections.body: Khác với các phương pháp truyền thống vốn yêu cầu người dùng tự soi đèn pin tìm điểm phản quang hoặc sử dụng camera quét hồng ngoại, vốn tốn thời gian và dễ nhầm lẫn với bề mặt kim loại, thủy tinh hay nhựa bóng, SweepLED giải quyết bài toán nhờ thuật toán deep learning.

sections.heading: Tác động thực tế với người đọc
sections.body: Theo Tom's Hardware , phụ kiện có thiết kế dạng lưới đèn LED, dễ dàng hít bằng nam châm vào mặt lưng smartphone. Khi hoạt động, hệ thống đèn liên tục thay đổi hướng chiếu sáng. Ánh sáng phản xạ từ các vật dụng thông thường sẽ di chuyển hoặc biến mất theo góc chiếu. Tuy nhiên, do cấu trúc quang học phức tạp gồm nhiều lớp thấu kính, khẩu độ và cảm biến ảnh, ống kính camera sẽ tạo ra một mô hình phản xạ ánh sáng rất đặc trưng khi chiếu từ nhiều góc độ khác nhau.

sections.heading: Ai nên chú ý lúc này
sections.body: Ứng dụng AI cài trên điện thoại sẽ phân tích biến đổi của mô hình phản xạ theo thời gian thực thay vì chỉ nhận diện một điểm sáng đơn lẻ. Trong thử nghiệm thực tế trên 30 vật dụng sinh hoạt quen thuộc như sạc điện thoại, đồng hồ báo thức, điều khiển từ xa và đồ trang trí, SweepLED đạt độ chính xác 93,9%, cho kết quả trong chưa đầy 5 giây.

sections.heading: Điều cần theo dõi tiếp
sections.body: Tình trạng lắp đặt camera quay lén tại các khu vực riêng tư như nhà vệ sinh, phòng thay đồ, nhà thuê hay phòng khách sạn đang trở thành nhức nhối tại nhiều quốc gia. Giáo sư Han Jun nhận định việc kết hợp phần cứng chi phí thấp với AI tạo ra một công cụ bảo vệ riêng tư tiện lợi, giúp ngay cả người không am hiểu công nghệ cũng có thể tự bảo vệ bản thân. Tuy nhiên, thời gian thương mại hóa phụ kiện chưa được nhóm nghiên cứu đề cập.

Tình trạng lắp đặt camera quay lén tại các khu vực riêng tư như nhà vệ sinh, phòng thay đồ, nhà thuê hay phòng khách sạn đang trở thành nhức nhối tại nhiều quốc gia. Giáo sư Han Jun nhận định việc kết hợp phần cứng chi phí thấp với AI tạo ra một công cụ bảo vệ riêng tư tiện lợi, giúp ngay cả người không am hiểu công nghệ cũng có thể tự bảo vệ bản thân. Tuy nhiên, thời gian thương mại hóa phụ kiện chưa được nhóm nghiên cứu đề cập.

Các chuyên gia cũng lưu ý công cụ có chi phí 7 USD này chỉ hỗ trợ phát hiện camera ẩn tại chỗ. Thiết bị không thể ngăn chặn rủi ro từ hàng chục nghìn camera an ninh hổng bảo mật đang phát trực tiếp dữ liệu công khai trên toàn cầu, hay sự phổ biến của các loại kính thông minh có khả năng ghi hình lén.

draft_context.source_title: Zuck's Muse to Spark joy with open weights release 'soon'
draft_context.description: Meta will release an open weights version of its flagship AI model Muse Spark "soon," CEO Mark Zuckerberg promised in an X post on Wednesday. In the meantime, Muse Spark 1.3 — the smarter, less yappy, and more efficient version of the model — is now live on the Facebook parent's API service and Muse Code CLI. Since releasing Muse Spark in April, Meta has released several refinements in order to keep pressure on the competition and convince investors its rampant capex isn't for naught. Version 1.3 brings several notable refinements, particularly for those using the model with AI agents and code assistants, which is welcome news considering OpenClaw 2.0 also dropped this week. According to Meta, the model should hold up better in "long-horizon" workloads and be a bit more realistic about what it can and can't do, rather than burning tokens repeatedly stumbling down dead-end paths. In particular, Meta says the model should seek human counsel more frequently when the correct path isn't clear. "Muse Spark 1.3 asks clarifying questions when prompts are ambiguous, invokes help from the user when stuck, and confirms before taking consequential actions," the Social Network explained in a blog post. These improvements also have the benefit of cutting down on the number of turns and tokens required to complete a task, which should make an already relatively affordable frontier model even less expensive to use. Compared to Muse 1.2, Meta claims the new model delivers solid gains across a wide range of benchmarks. Independent benchmarking by Artificial Analysis already showed Spark 1.2 to be quite competitive, delivering performance on par with GPT 5.6 Terra and Z.AI's GLM 5.3 Flash. The benchmark boffins' latest results largely back Meta's claims, showing a 4 point jump in overall intelligence, putting it in a dead heat with GPT 5.6 Sol, Claude Opus 5, and Grok 4.6 High. But if that's too steep for you and you don't mind lower rate limits or letting Meta rifle through your prompts for training data, its contributor tier offers steep discounts, down to $0.002 (cached input), $0.10 (input), and $0.20 (output) per million tokens. ®

sections.body: Nhưng Google không đơn thuần tung ra một model giá rẻ. Trên benchmark DeepSWE v1.1 dành cho kỹ thuật phần mềm dài hạn, Google cho biết Gemini 3.8 Flash có thể tự giải quyết các vấn đề kỹ thuật phức tạp từ đầu đến cuối và vượt qua phần lớn những frontier model lớn hơn, với chi phí chỉ bằng một phần.

sections.heading: Ai nên chú ý lúc này
sections.body: Cách Gemini 3.8 Flash xử lý các nhiệm vụ phức tạp cũng khác đáng kể so với một chatbot chỉ cố gắng đưa ra câu trả lời nhanh. sections.heading: Điều cần theo dõi tiếp

draft_context.source_title: Why your business can't trust the data behind its own security decisions
draft_context.description: When a critical vulnerability alert lands in a traditional IT environment, it’s rarely a cause for panic regarding the operational continuity of the business . The affected laptops, servers, and applications can be identified quickly, and a good team can catalogue and patch them within hours if it’s urgent. The priorities are clear, and there’s very little guesswork involved. Now picture the same alert landing across a hospital's imaging equipment, a factory floor's control systems, or a building's HVAC network. These cyber-physical systems (CPS), the connected devices that run physical operations rather than just processing data, sit at the sharp end of IT and OT (operational technology) convergence. But unlike traditional IT assets, confirming whether that alert even applies to a specific device can take days, and often ends in a guess rather than an answer. While this kind of uncertainty would be considered a failure of basic hygiene, for cyber-physical systems, it’s unfortunately much more often the norm. So why is this such a widespread problem for CPS, and how can security teams get these vital assets back in line with their IT network? Bad visibility into cyber-physical systems is worryingly widespread The inability to manage incoming vulnerabilities for CPS isn’t an outlier or worst-case scenario, which is especially concerning when these assets are at the heart of critical infrastructure like energy and healthcare. The issue comes down to the product codes that help networks identify what CPS is in the environment, which is an essential part of identifying and applying security patches. Across a dataset of 17 million cyber-physical assets, our research found that 88% failed to transmit an exact product code, and 76% sent a code that didn't match the vendor's own record. It’s a side effect of the way these systems were initially designed and later integrated into modern IT environments. Programmable logic controllers (PLCs), medical scanners, and industrial sensors were engineered for decades of physical reliability, not for tidy digital labeling. Network identification was rarely part of the design brief, so the same device can report itself differently depending on which protocol or integration is asking. We found a similar state of affairs when it comes to the operating systems behind the physical hardware . In our research, 41% of devices have no OS version available, and 24% have no OS name at all. Without these details, matching a device to a known vulnerability stops being a quick database lookup or automated process, and becomes a guessing game or painstaking manual search. Added to this, CVE advisories, the industry's standard mechanism for tracking vulnerabilities, are compiled from this same patchy vendor data. An official advisory can be just as incomplete as the network it's meant to protect. Translating product code chaos into boardroom risk This kind of blind spot adds another layer of concern to a leadership that is already anxious about threat visibility. Among 1,100 security leaders surveyed globally, 44% named understanding their organization's risk exposure as one of their biggest operational concerns, more than compliance pressure or budget constraints. A further 45% said they were struggling to reduce cyber risk to their most important assets and processes, yet the connection between that struggle and an unreliable asset inventory is often missed entirely. Leadership sees the symptom, a rising sense that risk is unmanageable, without ever seeing the cause sitting underneath it. This is where security and the business can end up talking past each other. Security teams that start describing the problem in terms of missing product codes and inconsistent naming conventions won’t get far. Business leaders hear none of that; they hear only that risk cannot be quantified with confidence. Until those two conversations are connected, every risk register that a CISO presents upward carries an asterisk that nobody in the room can see. Context is key to closing the gap Resolving this issue starts with a shift in what visibility means. Knowing a device exists on the network is only half of the job. Knowing what it does, what process depends on it, and what happens if it's compromised is what actually makes a risk register useful. Achieving this shift at scale requires specialized tools to manage the often eclectic and proprietary nature of CPS assets, and an automated approach to cope with the scale. In one example, applying AI-driven mapping techniques to an OEM's device catalogue lifted product code identification from 4% to 83%, turning a near-blind spot into a near-complete picture. The follow-through mattered just as much, with 56% of devices receiving a new or updated firmware recommendation as a result, and vulnerability identification accuracy improving by 25%. Numbers like these matter because they change the question security teams can answer. Instead of asking what's connected to the network, teams can ask which systems would cause the greatest disruption if compromised, and act on the answer with confidence rather than inference. That is the difference between an asset inventory that exists on paper and a resilient one that holds up under pressure. Fixing the foundation, not just the alarm None of this gets solved by adding another tool to the stack. Instead, it means treating asset data quality as a board-level risk issue rather than background IT housekeeping, with the same scrutiny applied to budgets, compliance and third-party access. Achieving this means a new CVE alert no longer triggers a scramble to work out which critical devices might be affected, but the confirmed, prioritized response you’d expect from any good vulnerability management program. The alert landing on a hospital's imaging equipment or a factory floor's control systems should be no harder to act on than the one landing on a laptop. Getting there starts with making the invisible visible. We've featured the best firewall software. draft_context.source_title: Apple iPhone Ultra vs. Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8: It could just come down to one thing
draft_context.description: Apple iPhone Ultra A bold new entrant The iPhone Ultra is set to usher in the age of the foldable iPhone, and leaks point to a device that has the potential to be truly noteworthy. Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Short and sweet The Z Fold 8 is uniquely interesting, and while it may not have the best cameras, it makes foldable fun to use. Apple iPhone Ultra vs. Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8: Pricing and availability (Image credit: Derrek Lee / Android Central) The iPhone Ultra is slated to make its debut at Apple's launch event on September 9, 2026. The foldable could cost anywhere between $2,000 to $2,500, and we'll have to wait until the event to know the official pricing. But with Apple hiking prices on most of its products in the last two months, it's a given that this year's iPhones will see price increases across the board. Even if the iPhone Ultra is unveiled alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, it may not actually show up at the same time — the latest leaks point to general availability later in the year. Again, that's something we will know definitely on September 9. Given the cost, it is projected that the foldable will be available in limited quantities — much like the Galaxy Z TriFold — and it remains to be seen if it will be sold in all regions simultaneously. Samsung unveiled the Galaxy Z Fold 8 on July 22, 2026, and the foldable retails at $1,899. This is the base model with 256GB of storage, and there's also a 512GB edition that costs $2,099 in the U.S., and a 1TB model that is $2,499. Apple iPhone Ultra vs. Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8: Design (Image credit: Nicholas Sutrich / Android Central) The iPhone Ultra will be different to every other iPhone thus far, with the foldable design ushering in an entirely new form factor for iOS. Leaks point to the iPhone Ultra having a similar wide-and-short configuration as the Galaxy Z Fold 8, and the passport-style design is definitely intriguing — there's no wonder that other Android manufacturers are emulating a similar style. Leaks point to a 5.5-inch cover panel and a 7.8-inch inner panel, and the iPhone Ultra could be as thin as 4.5mm while unfolded, bringing it in line with the Z Fold 8 and other Android foldables. The design looks a lot like the Pixel 11 Pro Fold , with rounded edges and a flatter profile along the hinge. While Apple introduced a bright orange color with the iPhone 17 Pro , the iPhone Ultra is said to be available in muted colors, including white and black. Just like Android foldables, the iPhone Ultra may see Touch ID housed within the power button as the standard mode of authentication instead of Face ID. The Z Fold 8 gets a 5.5-inch cover panel and a 7.6-inch inner screen, and Samsung managed to deliver IP48 dust and water resistance. Interestingly, one of the biggest selling points of the iPhone Ultra could be a display without anu visible crease. The Find N6 and Vivo X Fold 5 do a fabulous job in this regard — they're better than the Galaxy Z Fold 8 and Fold 8 Ultra — and with the iPhone Ultra touted to use two layers of ultra-thin glass and a liquid-metal hinge, it is entirely possible that Apple's foldable will debut with a creaseless design, outshining Samsung's Z Fold 8 in this key area. Apple iPhone Ultra vs. Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8: Hardware (Image credit: Apple / Android Central) The iPhone Ultra will see the biggest battery of any iPhone, and that in itself is exciting. Leaks point to a 4,883mAh battery, and that's similar to what's available on the Z Fold 8. That said, iOS has much better efficiency in general, so the iPhone Ultra should have better battery life, and with Apple touted to switch to a 2nm node, battery life could get an additional boost. Category Apple iPhone Ultra (based on leaks) Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Display Outer: 5.5-inch ProMotion LTPO OLED, 2088 x 1422 Inner: 7.8-inch ProMotion LTPO OLED Outer: 5.5-inch 120Hz LTPO AMOLED, 1972 x 1248 Inner: 7.6-inch 120Hz LTPO AMOLED, 2448 x 1848 Operating System iOS 27, at least seven updates One UI 9 (Android 17), seven updates Chipset Apple A20, 2nm Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy, 3nm RAM 12GB 12GB/16GB Storage 256GB, 512GB, 1TB, 2TB 256GB, 512GB, 1TB Rear cameras Main: 48MP f/1.8, sensor-shift OIS Wide-angle: 48MP f/2.2 Main: 50MP f/1.8, OIS Wide-angle: 50MP f/1.9 Front camera 24MP 10MP (internal), 10MP (external) Battery 4,883mAh 4,800mAh (dual 2,400mAh cells) Charging 40W iPhone 17 Pro, 25W MagSafe/Qi 2 45W wired, 20W wireless Dimensions Folded: 120.6 x 83.8 x 9.2mm Unfolded: 120.6 x 167.6 x 4.5mm Folded: 123.9 x 81.9 x 9.7mm Unfolded: 123.9 x 161.4 x 4.5mm Wide foldables are smaller than book-style devices like the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra , and as a result, Samsung just went with two cameras on the Galaxy Z Fold 8: a 50MP main camera and 50MP wide-angle lens. The iPhone Ultra is likely to use a similar arrangement, and leaks point to two 48MP cameras, without a dedicated tele lens. We'll need to wait and see if that pans out, but as someone who uses the telephoto lens constantly, I would like to see this on the foldable. Apple iPhone Ultra vs. Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8: Software (Image credit: Derrek Lee / Android Central) Software makes a big difference on a foldable, with the added real estate ideal to multitask. This is a priority in iOS 27, and there's no doubt that the iPhone Ultra will get a lot of the same features that we've seen on Android foldables over the last two years, including a task bar, floating windows, and multitasking features. Samsung does a good job in this area with the Galaxy Z Fold 8, and I'm interested in seeing how the iPhone Ultra will hold up against Samsung's foldable. Apple iPhone Ultra vs. Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8: Which should you buy? (Image credit: AppleTrack) While foldables have been around for the better part of a decade now, they're still pretty niche. That will change with the introduction of the iPhone Ultra; say what you will about Apple, but the brand has an unmatched ability to grab attention, and interest in foldables will skyrocket following the iPhone Ultra launch.
